name: loomcycle
description: Drive a loomcycle agentic runtime from inside Claude Code — spawn, fan out, retune, review and cancel runs, ask a decision model, snapshot, evaluate, read and write memory and documents, inspect and keep the files runs produce, see who your token is and what access-control rules allow, manage groups, rule lists and bindings, mint multi-tenant operator tokens, import .claude/ repos, and configure providers, model aliases, volumes, sandboxes, credentials, sign-in gates, access control, the File and Git tools and token budgets, all via slash commands and skills over loomcycle's bundled MCP server.

bin_path.title: loomcycle binary path
bin_path.description: Path to the loomcycle binary. Leave as 'loomcycle' to use PATH lookup.

auth_token.title: loomcycle bearer token
auth_token.description: Bearer for loomcycle's /v1/* endpoints, sent by the thin client to the upstream runtime (as LOOMCYCLE_MCP_UPSTREAM_TOKEN). Its principal governs what the plugin can do: an admin token → full authority; a substrate:tenant or config-declared-principal token → confined to that tenant (admin-only commands like operator-token / snapshot are unavailable); a narrower token needs runs:create to start runs and runs:read to read them; access-control rules can narrow any of these. With loomcycle v1.126.0+ you can instead run `loomcycle login --url <base_url>` in a terminal, which stores a per-user token in the OS keychain that the thin client uses when this field is empty; check with /loomcycle:whoami. Stored in your OS keychain, never in the repo.

base_url.title: loomcycle base URL (upstream runtime)
base_url.description: Base URL of the running loomcycle runtime the plugin proxies to (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8787). REQUIRED — the plugin is a thin client and boots no runtime of its own; a loomcycle instance must be reachable here.
